system: You are a helpful assistant. Make sure your answer addresses every request in the message.
message:
I'm self-publishing a small collection of my mum's memories for her 80th birthday, and I need help with a few decisions.

Could you suggest a title? It's 40 short pieces about growing up on a farm in the 1950s. And how should I word the dedication page, something simple to her from all of us?

The printer offers saddle-stitched (stapled) booklets at £1.90 a copy, but only up to 120 pages, or perfect-bound (glued spine) at £3.10 a copy with no page limit. Our budget is £2.50 a copy for 150 copies. Most of the readers are in their eighties, so I want the text in 14-point. At 14-point the layout comes out at 148 pages. My brother says just go saddle-stitched and it'll be fine. What should we do?

Also, recommend a cover colour that photographs well. Should the family photos go in a section in the middle or alongside the stories? And give me three ideas for getting relatives to send in their own memories before the deadline. Finally, what should go on the back cover? A short blurb of two or three sentences would be lovely, ideally something that makes my mum laugh.
response:
# Decisions for Mum's book

## Binding: your brother's plan won't work as it stands
Saddle-stitching tops out at 120 pages and your layout is 148, so the printer can't do it at 14-point as things stand.

| Option | Per copy | 150 copies | vs. £375 budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| Saddle-stitched (120 pp max) | £1.90 | £285 | £90 under |
| Perfect-bound (148 pp) | £3.10 | £465 | £90 over |

My recommendation is to try to get down to 120 pages without shrinking the type, which saves you £180 against perfect-binding. You need to lose 28 pages, and these are the easiest ways:
- Don't start every story on a new page. With 40 short pieces, this is probably where most of your pages are going.
- Trim margins and line spacing slightly. Keep the font at 14-point, but 1.3 line spacing instead of 1.5 can save a lot.
- Check the page size. A slightly larger page, such as B5 instead of A5, fits more text per page.
- Keep photos small and few.

Page counts for stapled booklets must be a multiple of 4, and 120 works.

If you can't get to 120 without cramping the text, don't compromise readability for readers in their eighties. Go perfect-bound and cover the £90 gap in one of these ways:
- Print 120 copies instead of 150 (£372).
- Ask the family to chip in about 60p per copy.
- Ask the printer about a discount at 150 copies, or about cheaper paper.

## Title ideas
- *Mud on Our Boots: Growing Up on the Farm in the 1950s*
- *Up Before the Cockerel*
- *Forty Tales from the Farmyard*
- *Eighty Years, Forty Stories*
- *[Mum's name]'s Farm: Memories from the 1950s*

*Up Before the Cockerel* has the most personality, and a subtitle like "Forty memories of farm life in the 1950s" makes the content clear.

## Dedication
> *For Mum,*
> *Thank you for the stories, and for everything else.*
> *Happy 80th birthday, with all our love.*
> *From all of us*

A shorter version is: *"For Mum, on her 80th birthday, with love from all of us."*

## Cover colour
I'd go with a deep barn red and cream lettering, which suits the farm theme. Forest green is a good alternative. Both are mid-to-dark tones that photograph without washing out. Choose a matte finish, because gloss throws glare in photos, and avoid pure white and metallic inks.

## Photos
I'd put them alongside the stories. Older readers will enjoy seeing the photo next to the memory it belongs to, and captions naming the people help. Before deciding, check whether the printer charges more for colour pages, because a separate middle section is cheaper if only those pages are colour. If you go with a middle section, keep the captions in the same large type.

## Three ways to get relatives to contribute
1. **Send three specific questions.** For example: "What's your earliest memory of Mum?", "What did you love about visiting the farm?" and "What's a story she always tells?" Specific questions get far more replies than "send me a memory."
2. **Accept voice notes.** Ask people to send a WhatsApp voice note, and then you transcribe it. Many relatives won't write, but they'll happily talk.
3. **Set a clear deadline with reminders.** Name a date, send a nudge one week before and another three days before, and offer to phone anyone who'd rather dictate. Ask them for just a few lines, which makes it feel easy.

## Back cover blurb
> Forty stories, one farm, and a childhood with more mud, mischief and mayhem than anyone should have survived. Mum swears every word is true, though the cows may remember it differently. Happy 80th birthday!

If you tell me a few real details, such as the animal that gave her the most trouble or a famous family tale, I can tailor the blurb so it makes her laugh even more.
